review_title: Greed has taken over this once awesome game.
review_text:
I’ve played Gardenscapes on and off for years, and it’s disappointing to see what this game has become. It used to be fun because there was a good balance of easy, medium, and hard levels. Some levels challenged you, some were relaxing, but overall it felt fair. You could actually make progress without feeling like you had to spend money.

Once you get past level 11,000, that balance is gone. Almost every level feels like a Hard or Super Hard level, even the ones that aren’t labeled that way. The difficulty feels intentionally increased to push players toward buying coins, boosters, and extra moves.

The coin rewards are also terrible. You can spend multiple lives and boosters trying to beat a difficult level, only to get rewarded with a small amount of coins that doesn’t come close to replacing what you used. The payout system makes progression feel like a constant struggle.

Gardenscapes has gone from a fun puzzle game to a pay-to-win cash grab. Instead of rewarding the players who have stuck with this game for years, the developers have made it more and more frustrating unless you’re willing to spend money.

It’s disappointing because this used to be one of my favorite games. After years of playing, I find myself enjoying it less and less because the focus seems to have shifted from creating a fun experience to finding more ways to get players to pay. Unless you’re willing to spend money, expect more frustration than fun.

review_text:
Ads

Chapter 1 is a masterclass on getting users to watch ads. Every ad provided real value and seriously accelerated progression. I treated the ads like mini games and blew through the first 100 levels easily. The game itself didn’t get that much play time as the ads contributed significantly. 

Chapter 2 was the same as chapter 1 but ads were no longer the only driving force. You got to choose which ads to watch because the value proposition dropped significantly.

Chapter 3 is entirely about game play. The value of the ads tanked and they’re only worth doing to complete the daily quests.

Gameplay
Chapters can be traversed and there is real value in going back to old chapters to quickly get items. The progression is exponential so after you get into chapter 2 you can go back to chapter 1 and have no fear of possibly dying.

Progression is super fast in chapter 1, only took me 3 days. Chapter 2 took 5 days. I can already tell that chapter 3 will take weeks.

The core loop of the game is best seen when you go to previous chapters. Run around the arena to kill monsters and get items. Collect all the chests and come back to them when the timer is up. After this core loop, you use the items collected to complete daily tasks like making weapons. There are some mini games like the challenge tower, boss raids, and invasions. None of the mini games are very valuable individually but combined with the events they are worth doing. The mini games are mostly deterministic at the start but later on there is some variety. For example, I can easily finish the second raid boss on expert mode but the first mini boss which has fewer requirements is basically impossible because the boss shield absorbs 300 hits regardless of how much damage they hit for. 

You have to finish the quest requirements in order to move on to the next chapter. This is a pain point because you can easily beat the chapter boss at 20 below and there is a slow tedious grind to level up. I am at level 204 right now and it feels like it would take several hours of auto play to get to 205. For the game to introduce itself as constant progression and a source of dopamine and then halt progression feels a bit icky. 

Purchases
I’ve bought the skip ads pack which claimed to remove all forced ads. It does help a lot but there have been a few times I left my phone to auto battle and came back to ad. The 5 ad skips a day are great but become less valuable as you progress through the game.

I also purchased the event pass for the new hero. I got kinda stuck where it would have taken me much longer to finish chapter 2 and I knew that the new hero would make it easier. Unfortunately, even though the purchase said guaranteed hero it didn’t just give me the hero outright, I still had to earn it which took a couple days. I would have preferred the purchase instantly gave me the materials required to unlock the hero and then any future materials could have been used to level it up. As it stands, the hero I purchased could have been earned normally and the price I paid for what I got doesn’t feel worth it. After this event, I don’t know how else I will get the materials required to level the hero up, which caps how strong it can get.

Lastly, everything you can purchase helps to a degree but there’s nothing that feels like purchasing it would get you past the next hard grind. I know this is pay to win I’m asking for but I’d rather get to the end game quickly and keep grinding in preparation for chapter 4 than to actively slog through.

Final thoughts
I really enjoyed the last week playing this game but I don’t plan to make any more purchases or watch a ton of ads. They simply aren’t rewarding enough at this stage. I’ll try the daily grind for an hour a day and see where that takes me. Overall, it’s certainly worth playing.

EDIT: After another week I went from 200 to 213 and I’m uninstalling. Even if I pay $100 I doubt it would get me through chapter 3. The progression is so bloody slow now I wish I uninstalled the game last week. 21 hours later and even more auto hunting and I am still exactly where I was last week. At 204 I could beat up to 250 bosses and that remains true at 213. To make matters worse, the invasion mini game is no longer just a time sink, it’s a time sink for even less rewards. The rewards that are given out after doing every daily challenge to the max and watching all the ads to get as much as possible is barely moving the needle. At this point my previous experience has been completely shadowed by an obvious money hungry paywall. It wasn’t worth noting before because auto hunting wasn’t really needed that much but the game is very demanding and absolutely drains the battery. Download the game, beat the first two chapters and don’t look back. I really wanted to see the other areas because this game’s art style and enemy variety is pretty neat but it’s not worth spending thousands to do so. Genuinely, if they let me get to end game and grind for the 4th chapter I would have spent way more money on this game but with this exponential requirement increase I’m not having fun anymore and there’s no point.

review_title: First game is great - second, not so much.
review_text:
TLDR; No warnings of AI use, frustrating endings, and weird visuals for the second game.

The title is exactly what this review is about.

The first game was genuinely phenomenal. Great storyline along with choices, and amazing visuals. I played it multiple times over just to see where the story goes if I make this choice vs. this choice, and obviously, the visuals. (trying not to give spoilers lol) Really, really happy with this game.

The second? 

I hated it. Not immediately, it slowly built up throughout the game.

1st. The visuals looked… kinda different this time around. I can’t put my finger on it, but I just didn’t like it compared to the first. Whatever. I kept playing, not a huge deal.

2nd. I started to notice how dumb some of the endings were. “Haha, you shouldn’t have done that!” For something as tiny as picking up a cup or something. Obviously the first game had its fair share of endings that I would consider “dumb”, but never to this extent and never this many. I moved on and kept playing, though annoyed.

3rd. I finally got down to an ending. Not a good one, but still an ending. You wanna know what the first thing I noticed was? Entire ending was made by AI. Legitimately the entire thing.

Now, this was a text ending. I got real used to these since they appeared throughout the entire game, with the text appearing on the BLACK screen (you know, like a normal game 😒). But this time, it had actual scenes behind it that were entirely “curated” by AI, that could’ve easily just been the same black screen the rest of the game had.

I noticed this afterwards, but at least a majority of the captions also were likely created by AI.

That was the straw that broke the camel’s back.

Yet here we are. This is by far one of the worst games I’ve ever played and it’s purely cause of the sheer greed. You want 50 dollars from me? Make a game worth that 50 dollars and not this microtransaction bs.
